guards.what: N1: `return player != base.Owner;` (Sozu.cs:17-20) vs the sim's unconditional `return False` (sozu.py:27); and the same missing owner check on ModifyMaxEnergy (Sozu.cs:24-27)
guards.rationale: Both are multiplayer owner filters. C#'s ShouldProcurePotion is dispatched over every listener in the run including other players' relics, so `player != Owner` means 'only refuse MY potions'; with one player that expression is constantly False, which is exactly what sozu.py:27 returns. The sim's own hook signature has no player parameter at all (relics/base.py:217-220), so the distinction is unrepresentable and unneeded. Waived as multiplayer-only under the shared contract's global scope, not under an unreachability claim about ported content.
